d.d: The pointing of a weapon, as a gun, a dart, or an arrow, or object, in the line of direction with the object intended to be struck; the line of fire; the direction of anything, such as a spear, a blow, a discourse, a remark, towards a particular point or object, with a view to strike or affect it.
The level of accuracy of a weapon.
d.x: A rifle has more precise aim than a shotgun.

d.d: The point intended to be hit, or object intended to be attained or affected.
To point or direct a missile, or a weapon which propels as missile, towards an object or spot with the intent of hitting it
d.x: He aimed at the target, but the arrow flew straight over it.

d.d: To direct the intention or purpose; to attempt the accomplishment of a purpose; to try to gain; to endeavor;—followed by at, or by an infinitive
To direct or point (e.g. a weapon), at a particular object; to direct, as a missile, an act, or a proceeding, at, to, or against an object
d.x: to aim an arrow at the deer

One who aims; one who is responsible for aiming.
present participle and gerund of aim
present participle and gerund of AIM
The act of one who aims.
Without an aim, purpose or direction; in an aimless manner.
d.x: He wandered aimlessly through the crowd.
